items.title: The first real Rewrite play
items.summary: Rewrite support is built and tested against the client's source. A genuine Rewrite 0.1.2 replay going all the way through will prove it end to end.

items.title: Automatic bans
items.summary: Flagged plays always go to a person.

items.title: Faye gets her own Discord presence and chats in the server
items.summary: Faye gets her own Discord account so people can talk to her in the server and she answers, with the same memory and files she works from today. Cole said yes on 3 Oct; the setup is under way on his PC.

items.title: Revisiting provisional values
items.summary: HardRock, Flashlight, Nearsighted and the miss weighting are first guesses. We'll review them once more players have submitted.

items.title: A custom domain for the website
items.summary: Serve the website from its own short address instead of the GitHub Pages one.

items.title: Suggestions for the Rewrite client
items.summary: Ask the client's developers to store the map's note hash in replays, and to use a random replay ID instead of one tied to the PC.

items.title: More progression systems
items.summary: Quests, seasons and streak rewards. The profile level and medals stay, but the ranking is only about plays.

items.title: The bot's profile text names both clients, like the website does
items.summary: The bot's Discord profile said it was for Sound Space Plus only, while the website says Rhythia's Nightly and Rewrite clients. The profile now says the same as the website.

items.title: Songs for more maps
items.summary: A curator can let the website play a map's song with its replays; maps nobody has said yes to still play silently.

items.title: The replay viewer says a curator can share a map's song
items.summary: When a map's song is not on the site, the viewer offered only your own maps folder or a map file. It now also says that a curator can share the song so it plays for everyone, so a player knows to ask.

items.title: The compare page's shared-maps table fits a phone
items.summary: On a phone the second player's column scrolled off the edge. The star pill now sits under the map's title and the cells are tighter, so the map and both players' PP fit side by side.

items.title: Wider copied-replay checking
items.summary: Copied replays are checked against more of a map's earlier plays.

items.title: A patch reaches main, then nothing else to do: bot, website and channels follow
items.summary: When a release reaches main, the bot, the website and the Discord channels should follow on their own within seconds, with one line in server-logs saying what updated.

items.title: A tidier card for a failed run
items.summary: The score card for a failed run says so without its caption running into the grade badge.

items.title: Held plays keep their reasons private
items.summary: When a play is held for a curator's check, the public reply only says it is being checked; the reasons go to the curators, not to the channel.

items.title: A clear route from the home page to the submit steps
items.summary: The home page links straight to how to submit, the empty podium spots do too, and the public site's tab says "How to submit".

items.title: A how-to-submit walkthrough
items.summary: Illustrated steps on the Submit page that show finding the replay and sending it in, drawn so no recording is needed.

items.title: Play rows wrap on a phone
items.summary: A play's details (grade, stars, speed, time) wrap to a second line instead of being cut off.

items.title: A security check of the website server
items.summary: A careful read through everything the local web server can show, to make sure nothing private can be reached.

items.title: A quieter login button
items.summary: Logging in on the website only highlights your own plays. The button now looks like it, and the header is two tidy rows on a phone.

items.title: The website's styles are tidied after the redesign (no visible change)
items.summary: The redesign shipped as a second set of rules layered over the old ones. They are now one set, so the stylesheet is simpler to work on. Every page renders the same as before.

items.title: A map page's speed rows fit a phone
items.summary: On a phone the two rows of speed buttons ran off the right edge of the map's header, so Nightly's fastest speeds could not be reached. Each row now stays inside the header and swipes sideways.

items.title: A shorter Maps page on a phone
items.summary: Maps show two to a row on a phone, with a "Show more" button instead of every map at once.

items.title: A friendlier profile before your first ranked play
items.summary: A profile with no ranked plays yet shows dashes and a hint, instead of zeros that look like a bug.

items.title: Helpful not-found pages
items.summary: A wrong or old link now says what wasn't found and where to go, and a page that fails to load offers a retry.

items.title: A loading line while a page fetches
items.summary: A short "Loading…" shows while a page's data arrives, so nothing looks broken on a slow connection.

items.title: A permanent home for the data
items.summary: Moving the bot's leaderboard data to its permanent place, then watching what real plays show up.

items.title: Tabs that show they scroll on a phone
items.summary: The tab row fades where it continues, and the tab you're on scrolls into view.

items.title: The level on a player page has no label
items.summary: A player page shows a hexagon with a number and a bar with a percentage, with no word saying it's the level. The explanation is a hover tooltip, which a phone can't show.

items.title: The challenge pool table explained
items.summary: The pool page says what its Sheet and Stars columns mean.

items.title: A shorter challenge-sheet page: search, and 20 maps per tier with Show more
items.summary: The sheet page listed all 500-odd maps at once, which on a phone is minutes of scrolling. Now a search box finds a map or mapper, and each tier shows 20 rows with a Show more button.

items.title: A play's PP is its own; the weighted figure is what it adds to the total
items.summary: Best plays showed '198pp · 95% → 188pp', which reads as if the play were worth less. Now the play's PP stands alone and the small line says 'counts 188pp · 95%': what it adds to your total.

items.title: A big blank where the rank graph will be
items.summary: Until a player has two days of history, the rank graph's space on their page is a single muted line ("The rank graph fills in day by day") above a large empty area, so the top of the page looks unfinished.

items.title: Repeated attempts grouped on a player page
items.summary: Retrying one map many times no longer fills your Recent list: the attempts are grouped into one row.

items.title: Resubmitting says what to do
items.summary: Send a new run of the same map as often as you like to beat your score. Only the exact same replay file is refused, and the message now says so.

items.title: Easier with a screen reader
items.summary: After you open a page, a screen reader hears its title instead of the whole page.

items.title: Rows and tables that show they scroll on a phone
items.summary: Wide tables and a player page's section row fade at the edge they continue past, instead of looking cut off.

items.title: A stale link to a map, player or play lands on the site's own not-found page
items.summary: A link to a map, player or play that is no longer on the site currently drops you on the home page with no word. It should land on the site's own 'not found' page, which says what happened and where to go.

items.title: The stats page's weekly chart is readable on a phone
items.summary: The week labels under the plays-per-week chart were about 9 px tall on a phone. They are now about 14 px, the same size as the rest of the page's small text.

items.title: "1 NEW PLAYERS THIS WEEK" on the Stats page
items.summary: The Stats page's tiles say "1 NEW PLAYERS THIS WEEK" and would say "1 PLAYS THIS WEEK": the labels are fixed text while the numbers change.

items.title: The Submit page is a proper how-to
items.summary: It says which maps count, where to run the command, what to do if the bot doesn't know your map, and what the bot's reply means.

items.title: A Top plays row opens two different things
items.summary: Top plays says "click one to watch it", but tapping the map name opens the map while tapping anywhere else opens the replay. On a phone the Watch button is hidden, so nothing marks the replay as the row's target.

items.title: A play on an unranked map says how to nominate it
items.summary: When your play lands on a map that isn't ranked, the bot's reply tells you how to nominate it.

items.title: A look at the bot's replies
items.summary: We read every reply and card the bot can send for anything unclear to a player. The fixes are their own items.

items.title: A look at a new player's first play
items.summary: We followed the path from "I want to play" to a first verified play and listed where a newcomer gets lost. The fixes are their own items.

items.title: A look at every website page
items.summary: We went through every page on a phone and a desktop for anything confusing, ugly or hard to use. The fixes are their own items.

items.title: The welcome post points to the ranked map list
items.summary: The Discord welcome and /help send you to the website's Maps page for the list of ranked maps, and say the bot replies to every submit.

items.title: Easier to read and use
items.summary: Stronger contrast, and charts, search boxes and tables labelled for screen readers.

items.title: Compare two players
items.summary: On the website and with /compare in Discord: the maps you both played, who is ahead on each, and the biggest gaps.

items.title: A guard against the wrong data
items.summary: If the bot ever starts on the wrong database, it pauses instead of publishing an empty leaderboard.

items.title: Double-sending a replay is handled
items.summary: Sending the same replay twice at once saves it once and says so, instead of showing an error.

items.title: Map of the week
items.summary: The Monday roundup spotlights one ranked challenge-sheet map, taking each in turn.

items.title: A star filter on the Maps page
items.summary: Narrow the list to under 3★, 3–5★, 5–7★ or 7★+.

items.title: Nomination status for players
items.summary: After /nominate, players can see where their nominated map stands.

items.title: The website says when the bot is offline
items.summary: If the site hasn't heard from the bot in a few hours, every page says so.

items.title: A heads-up when the formula changes
items.summary: If everyone is re-scored, the Discord gets a short note with the biggest rank changes.

items.title: A public roadmap
items.summary: This page: what is being worked on, what is next, and what is finished.

items.title: Community stats page
items.summary: Plays and players per week, and Nightly versus Rewrite.

items.title: An alert when the bot goes offline
items.summary: If the bot's PC goes offline, an outside service messages the owner within minutes, instead of the website only saying so after hours.

items.title: Website buttons in Discord
items.summary: Every result, profile, map and #1 post links to the website.

items.title: An archive of weekly roundups
items.summary: Past weekly roundups, kept on the website so anyone can look back.

items.title: The challenge pool
items.summary: Maps on the community sheet are ranked automatically, and anyone can /nominate a map.

items.title: Daily backups
items.summary: The database and every replay are backed up each day, checked, and kept for a year.

items.title: Score cards, roles, medals and a weekly roundup
items.summary: The Discord bot scores each play the moment it's sent in.

items.title: Fair play checks
items.summary: Every replay is re-verified, suspicious plays are held for a person, and copied replays and shared PCs are refused.

items.title: The bot reconnects to Discord by itself
items.summary: A dropped or silent connection is given up on and re-opened without anyone doing anything.

items.title: Star ratings and PP for Nightly and Rewrite
items.summary: One shared, replay-backed ranking for both clients.

items.title: The bot updates itself
items.summary: New versions arrive from GitHub within minutes, tests run first, and a version that will not start is undone automatically.

items.title: Rankings, map and player pages, and a replay viewer
items.summary: The website, with a replay viewer that looks like the game.
